name: Ukraine
summary_text: Ukraine is workable for trans visitors, with the caveat that this scores trans-specific risk, not the obvious general risks of an active war zone. Ukraine criminalises nothing about being trans; legal gender recognition exists (medicalised — a "transsexualism" diagnosis and psychiatric observation under the 2016 protocol), and a resilient civil society (Gender Stream, Insight) operates openly. Kyiv hosted a three-day Trans Forum in June 2026 even during the war. Trans-specific frictions exist but mostly affect residents, not visitors: trans women with male passports cannot leave the country under martial law (conscription), and wartime document checks can out people. A foreign visitor's passport is not subject to mobilisation rules, so border crossing is governed by standard wartime entry rules. There is no SOGI-specific hate-crime law, societal attitudes lag EU averages, and the healthcare system is war-disrupted (hormone shortages, diagnostic corruption reported). Ukraine scores far above Russia (0.12) and Belarus (0.13) — no criminalisation, no state persecution, functioning NGOs — and below Serbia (0.64) and Moldova (0.65), reflecting wartime institutional strain and weaker legal protections rather than active hostility.

sources.title: When Laws Fail to Protect Trans People, Harmful Medicalized Norms Creep In | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch essay (May 2024): 'When Laws Fail to Protect Trans People, Harmful Medicalized Norms Creep In' — examines Ukraine's LGR regime requiring a 'transsexualism' diagnosis and humiliating military-medical-commission confirmation, worsened by wartime displacement.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying France24 piece (June 2022) covers Ukraine's trans community caught in the crosshairs of war.

sources.title: Trans women now find it more difficult to obtain a diagnosis: Stereotypes, corruption and other challenges facing transgender people during wartime ➜ ZMINA
sources.claim_summary: ZMINA (July 2026): 'Trans women now find it more difficult to obtain a diagnosis' - stereotypes, corruption and other challenges facing transgender people during wartime; interviews from Trans Forum 2026 in Kyiv covering corruption in healthcare, hormone-medication shortages, mobilisation-related problems, risks of the new draft Civil Code, the legal gender-change process, and the transition to ICD-11.

sources.title: Consultations and support - Gender Stream
sources.claim_summary: Gender Stream (Ukrainian NGO): consultations and support - advises and accompanies LGBTQI+ people and families during evacuation from combat regions to western Ukraine and the EU; helps with processing/reissuing documents for trans people and legal border crossing; monitors human-rights observance during document processing and travel abroad under martial-law restrictions.

European Parliament written question E-002018/2022 (Jun 2022): on the situation of transgender people in Ukraine amid the Russian invasion, in the context of Parliament's resolution on war's impact on women.

sources.title: Ukraine: Discrimination and violent attacks in pervasive climate of homophobia - Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International (May 2013): 'Ukraine: Discrimination and violent attacks in pervasive climate of homophobia' - report 'Nothing to be proud of' exposes endemic discrimination; people beaten and one murdered; most crimes uninvestigated; the possibility of attack used as an excuse to deprive LGBTI people of assembly rights; lawmakers urged to reject 'propaganda' bills.

sources.title: Good news from Malaysia, Namibia, Ukraine
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Aug 2016): 'Good news from Malaysia, Namibia, Ukraine' - advances for trans people in Ukraine (alongside Malaysia's ID-card ruling and Namibia's ombudsman comments) per ILGA's LGBulleTIn round-up.

sources.title: Ukraine: Investigate Brutal Attack on Gay Activist | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (June 2012): 'Ukraine: Investigate Brutal Attack on Gay Activist' - documents the violent attack on an LGBT activist and calls for investigation amid the 'propaganda' bill debates.
